# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 22:03 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 247 active entries of tips_notebook.json (46 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote, and flag any stated vote that changes or that the totals contradict (e.g. more Guilty votes than players who said Guilty). Make your own ballot match your stated read, and explain any change before the vote. (seen in 30 games)
- You can't use tokens once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, ritual guess, shots, swaps) on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die that night, so spend it at least a night before a likely death. (seen in 18 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: a watch can't tell protection from a frame or an attack. But if a corroborated Lookout shows X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, and don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X. (seen in 29 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical contradiction, such as a broken claim, an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination or a lone visitor. A role-block fully explains a missing result, roles can repeat unless proven unique, and a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 32 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will. Results from the night you die never reach your will, so post every result publicly by day. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. A dodge, or a denial you later reverse, becomes the case against you. (seen in 15 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies you. A held-back result looks retrofitted. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is mechanically shown Yakuza, suspect those who defended them or argued to delay. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the totals; a No on the nomination followed by Guilty once the hang is certain is the telling pattern. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link or a pile of soft leans is a lead, never a hang: Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. Require a mechanical result before convicting. (seen in 28 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers from Day 2. Read every cause of death: an ignite or Serial Killer attack proves that killer is alive. Keep a written suspect list (unwatched Vanilla claimants, players who survived attacks with no credible protector, unexplained visit gaps) and spend a hang on the best suspect before the endgame, because at two alive you can't hang them. (seen in 17 games)
- Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged: watch for self-nominations, eager-to-be-tried claims and easily disproved fake results. If you must hang a possible Jester, keep Guilty votes to a bare majority and have confirmed power roles vote Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Surviving an attack confirms nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor what explains their Defense, and test the answer with an audit or a watch. (seen in 15 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually stop the hang; otherwise vote Guilty and say so. On a likely Jester, keep some of you on Innocent, because every Guilty voter is in the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never PM teammates by day: an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads it, and a visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead. Plan in night chat. (seen in 30 games)
- Agree a fake claim in night chat before Day 2 that fits your token count and real visits. Never claim a Yakuza-only role or a unique role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night once a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. After a failed attack, remove the protector instead of retrying. (seen in 21 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive an attack, nobody else knows you were targeted, so don't announce it. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and keep it. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing; say so when you post it. Once only one Yakuza can be alive, no Not Evil result clears anyone. (seen in 16 games)

## Medic
- Your free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it on vocal analysts and claimed investigators, and rotate rather than follow a predictable pattern. Self-protect with a token the night you claim, and never say you 'confirmed' a save, since you get no feedback. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot on a lead, not proof: a claim conflict, an Evil result against an unverifiable claim, or a defender of an exposed Yakuza. Dying with all your tokens is the usual failure. A failed Basic shot hints at innate Defense, so post it. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a townie can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, never when a teammate is the likely nominee. On the rigged trial, teammates vote Innocent, because a small Guilty total exposes them. (seen in 18 games)

## Smuggler
- A swap moves exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players, so don't veto it out of fear. To beat a Medic, aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with your real target. To dodge a check, swap yourself with a Villager. Never swap the target unless you mean to move the kill, and have a cover ready for both swap visits. (seen in 7 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused, or 2 if you're being questioned. Douse players likely to survive, not today's hang targets. (seen in 12 games)

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Once the Katana holder has been attacked and survived, consider moving the Katana the same night; a repeated attack on a Medic-protected target just wastes the kill while the Medic keeps protecting them.
Don't let teammates argue the same lines in public defences of each other; identical phrasing across defences (as with Frank, Erin and Grace) makes the whole team a single readable target.

A Sheriff's single Evil read with no second check should not be enough to hang someone; before a trial, demand the Sheriff's log or a corroborating visit, and track which players voted Innocent on earlier hangs.
Insomniac logs show roles, not targets, so they confirm that a Sheriff or Medic visited someone but not who; don't treat them as proof of a specific claim.

Avoid PM-ing teammates or pushing your own hang-argument through private chats; a visible private message trail between two players (Frank->Bob, Erin->Bob) was used as the town's lead against the Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Never PM teammates by day: an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads it, and a visible PM triangle becomes the town's lead. Plan in night chat.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's and Erin's private messages to Bob were visible as a PM trail and Bob cited them publicly to nominate Grace, which exposed the Yakuza's pressure on Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night; with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Our Night 3 votes all matched, so the Katana kill on Heidi went through.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually stop the hang; otherwise vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Our Innocent defences of Frank and Erin were repeated and predictable, and this pattern made Grace the next nominee once the trial pressure built.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a player is mechanically shown Yakuza, suspect those who defended them or argued to delay.
tips_feedback.why: Town used the repeated Innocent-and-delay pattern from Frank and Erin to target Grace, so the defence pattern was predictable and cost us the Grunt.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night once a Lookout or Tracker names the holder.
tips_feedback.why: Only the holder is the Katana, and keeping it with Grace (the last Yakuza) meant there was no reserve holder; the tip assumes teammates remain alive to receive the Katana.

lessons.tip: Insomniac output shows roles of visitors, not targets; a visit of a real Sheriff cannot be tied to a specific player, so do not treat a visitor count as proof a claimed Sheriff acted on a particular person. Post the exact visitor roles and state explicitly what they cannot prove.

Do not vote Guilty on one unverified investigative read when the claimant's own later claims keep changing targets; demand the target and log before each hang, and prefer a hang only once a second independent check exists.

Track each player's stated votes against announced totals and against private PM contents; here the hang chain (Frank, Erin, Grace) was driven by one Sheriff read and PM contents, and nobody checked whether the Sheriff's claim was the Yakuza's bait.

Yakuza who keep submitting the same Katana holder and target every night with a Grunt inside can be exposed by any visitor log; keep a Katana holder who is a non-Grunt role if possible and avoid stacking multiple visits on one night.
Avoid echoing the same defence lines across trials; repeated phrasing across consecutive defences of different players became the main public tell that pointed to the Yakuza pair.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical contradiction, such as a broken claim, an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination or a lone visitor.
tips_feedback.why: Players who demanded a concrete contradiction (Frank, Erin, Grace) forced the Sheriff to commit to specific targets, which exposed the shifting claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the totals; a No on the nomination followed by Guilty once the hang is certain is the telling pattern.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's audits and stated-vote comparison caught Bob's walk-back and tied the Yes voters to the announced 4 Yes total.

tips_feedback.tip: A PM link or a pile of soft leans is a lead, never a hang: Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. Require a mechanical result before convicting.
tips_feedback.why: Bob nominated Grace on the strength of PM contents he alone could see, and that hang was driven by PM links; a mechanical result was not required, so the rule was not followed by the group.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at a power role on Day 1. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: Every public Katana-relevant claim from the Yakuza side stayed vague, so the Katana target was never pre-announced to them by a Medic or Sheriff.

summary: Village won cleanly. Dave (Sheriff) checked Frank (Fixer) on Night 1 and got Evil, and posted it on Day 2. Heidi's Insomniac result (only a Medic and a Sheriff visited on N1) backed Dave's visit and ruled out a Fabricator frame or an Ex-Con visit. Alice backed it up by claiming the Medic visit. The Yakuza then made three linked mistakes. First, all three claimed Vanilla Villager, repeated each other's 'one Sheriff read isn't enough' lines, and voted No/Innocent as a bloc. That put them in a visible 3-vote block. Second, Frank never used either Fixer token. His Day 3 trial ended 5-3 Guilty, so fixing one Guilty voter the night before would have made it 4-4 and saved him; he died holding both tokens. Third, Alice openly said she would protect a claimed power role. The Yakuza still hit Dave on N2, where Alice's protection stopped them, and then killed Heidi on N3, an Insomniac with no tokens left, instead of Alice. On N4 Grace hit Dave again and Alice blocked it again. Meanwhile Dave's N3 Evil result on Erin got her hanged, and the 'defended both hanged Yakuza and voted Innocent each time' pattern hanged Grace. Grace's N4 Not Evil came only from holding the Katana, which Dave correctly flagged.

lessons.tip: Count the likely trial vote before the night and fix a pro-hang voter whenever one flipped vote breaks the Guilty majority, especially to save an exposed teammate. Don't hoard tokens 'for a trial that matters'. The trial on your own exposed teammate is that trial.
lessons.evidence: Frank was read Evil on N1 and the Day 2 nomination already drew 4 Yes. He kept both fixer tokens on N2 and was hanged 5 Guilty to 3 Innocent on Day 3. A single fixed Guilty voter (Bob, Heidi or Alice) would have made it 4-4, and he would have survived.

lessons.tip: Don't all claim Vanilla Villager, and don't defend a teammate with the same talking points and the same votes. Spread your claims, word your arguments differently, and when a teammate is clearly doomed and you can't swing the vote, have at least one member vote Guilty so you don't form a visible bloc.
lessons.evidence: Erin, Frank and Grace all claimed Vanilla, so half the table claimed Vanilla, and all three repeated 'name a second check / one Sheriff read isn't enough' and voted No/Innocent. Carol and Bob hanged Erin and then Grace mainly because 'her defence repeated Frank's lines' and 'Innocent on both Frank and Erin'.

lessons.tip: After a Katana attack fails on a likely-protected target, kill the protector next, not a spent information role, and don't retry the same protected player. Rank kills by how much a player can still do, not by what they already revealed.
lessons.evidence: Alice announced she would protect a claimed power role, and the N2 attack on Dave failed. On N3 the Yakuza killed Heidi, who had 0 insomniac tokens left. On N4 Grace attacked Dave again, and Alice stopped it again. Alice was never targeted, and Dave's result on Erin and the push against Grace went ahead.

lessons.tip: Combine visit-role information with alignment checks. An Insomniac or Lookout result showing no Fabricator or Ex-Con visit means a Sheriff's Evil result can't be a frame. Then an Evil result on a Vanilla claimant is a real mechanical contradiction worth hanging on.
lessons.evidence: Heidi's N1 'Medic, Sheriff' result, plus Alice claiming the Medic visit, left Dave's Evil read on Frank as the only explanation. Carol and Dave used exactly that ('a Vanilla can't read Evil, and no frame was possible') to win the Day 3 vote.

lessons.tip: Post every new result, with target and outcome, in your first message each Day, before any nomination. Results revealed late or during a trial let opponents claim your story is growing. When you post a Not Evil result on a suspected Katana holder, say plainly that it clears nothing.
lessons.evidence: Dave held back his N2 target on Day 2 and posted N3 and N4 only alongside nominations or trials. Erin and Grace attacked this: 'his claims have grown every day' and 'N4 result first appeared after Bob nominated me'. Dave correctly noted that the holder reads Good, and Grace was still hanged.

lessons.tip: Once a Sheriff is corroborated and the Yakuza have shown they target him, keep protecting him with your free Standard protection. The Katana is only Standard, so each repeat save keeps the town's best information source alive.
lessons.evidence: Alice protected Dave on N2, N3 and N4. The Katana attacks on N2 and N4 both failed, and Dave lived to read Erin as Evil on N3.

lessons.tip: Nominate only when the Yes votes are clearly there; count stated Yes votes first. A failed nomination followed by a public walk-back wastes the round and makes you a target of suspicion.
lessons.evidence: Bob nominated Frank on Day 2 with only 4 Yes votes (5 needed), then publicly retracted his Yes. That gave the Yakuza ammunition against Bob for several days. Frank was hanged anyway on Day 3, once the case was stronger.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical contradiction, such as a broken claim, an Evil result against a Vanilla claim...
tips_feedback.why: The Village built its case on the 'Evil result against a Vanilla claim' contradiction, backed by Heidi's frame-free visit log. The Yakuza's repeated 'name one mechanical contradiction' demands didn't hold up against it.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a player is mechanically shown Yakuza, suspect those who defended them or argued to delay.
tips_feedback.why: After Frank was hanged, the town turned on Erin and then Grace for defending him and voting Innocent. Both were Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Sheriff: The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing; say so when you post it.
tips_feedback.why: Dave flagged that Grace's N4 Not Evil could mean she held the Katana, which she did. The other villagers ignored the result and hanged her.

tips_feedback.tip: Medic: Your free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it on vocal analysts and claimed investigators...
tips_feedback.why: Alice put her free Standard protection on Dave every night from N2 to N4 and stopped the Katana on N2 and N4, keeping the Sheriff alive.

tips_feedback.tip: You can't use tokens once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens ... on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat.
tips_feedback.why: Frank ignored it and died with both fixer tokens unused. One fix the night before his trial would have made the vote 4-4 and saved him, so following the tip would have helped the Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually stop the hang; otherwise vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored it. All three defended Frank and voted Innocent, and that bloc became the main evidence used to hang Erin and Grace.

tips_feedback.tip: Give the Katana to a low-value member ... After a failed attack, remove the protector instead of retrying.
tips_feedback.why: Not followed. After the N2 save, the Yakuza never attacked Alice and wasted N4 retrying Dave; following the tip would have removed the Sheriff's protection.

issues.description: On Days 2 and 3, several Village players (Bob, Dave, Heidi, Alice) said Heidi's Insomniac log showed 'a real Sheriff visit on Frank'. The Insomniac learns only the roles of visitors, not their targets. Frank and Grace pointed this out during the trial, and Heidi then admitted it. Some votes were justified with this mistaken reading.

Players misread the Auditor's scope. On Day 2 Carol said 'anyone who casts a nomination vote today will be checked', and on Day 3 Erin asked Carol to 'post your audit on each Yes voter'. The Auditor audits only one player per night. Carol's post-game feedback also said the auditor result's scope was hard to pin down.
Carol's debrief said the speaking-budget rules were hard to pin down and asked for a worked example or a per-turn budget readout. This suggests the players' budget information is unclear.
